report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. Clinical trial data and public health consensus demonstrate that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV / Shingrix) significantly reduces the risk of shingles in adults aged 70 years or older.

**Key Evidence:**

1. **Pivotal Phase 3 Trial (ZOE-70):** A randomized, placebo-controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated RZV in nearly 14,000 adults aged 70 and older. The vaccine demonstrated approximately 90% efficacy against herpes zoster, reducing incidence from 9.2 cases per 1,000 person-years in the placebo group to 0.9 per 1,000 person-years in the vaccine group (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800).

2. **Public Health Consensus:** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends RZV for all adults aged 50 and older, noting that high level protection persists for at least seven years following vaccination in adults aged 70 and older (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/vaccines/index.html).

3. **Superiority to Older Vaccines:** Clinical reviews published by the American Academy of Family Physicians highlight that RZV achieves high efficacy in older age brackets where older, live-attenuated vaccines previously showed declining protection (https://www.aafp.org/afp/2018/1015/p539).

In summary, the scientific evidence does not support the view that the vaccine is ineffective in this population; rather, it provides around 90% protection against shingles for adults 70 years and older.
